old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

independent_computation.step_0_scope_note: The scenario id 'syndra_derived_order_39' appears nowhere under data/ (grepped data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json and all of data/) - it is engine-generated, and item_coverage[0] is whichever item sits first in derived order permutation 39. The item name is therefore not resolvable from the evidence tree. Instead of guessing one item, I enumerated EVERY item a Summoner's Rift Syndra (MAGE-tagged, EPIC/LEGENDARY, not removed) can hold whose entire effect content is a defence - i.e. the complete set of items that could legitimately carry this reason - and checked both sentences against each of them.

step_1_candidate_enumeration.method: For each item in data/items.json with shop.tags containing MAGE and rank in {EPIC, LEGENDARY}, take the set of declared atom families from data/item-atoms/<id>.json, excluding the pure 'stats' block.
step_1_candidate_enumeration.note: Stat-only mage items (Kindlegem, Giant's Belt, Fiendish Codex, Void Staff, Blighting Jewel) declare no effect families at all, so they cannot carry a 'represented mechanic' reason.

step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.Annul (Banshee's Veil 3102, Verdant Barr: Cached wiki branch text: 'Grants a spell shield that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown, timer restarts upon taking damage from champions).' The mechanic consumes a HOSTILE ability aimed at the holder. There is no on-hit, on-cast, amplification, penetration, or proc term - it contributes exactly 0 to any outgoing damage sum. Its contribution is to durability: it removes one incoming instance.
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.Time Stop (Zhonya's 3157, Seeker's Armgu: Cached wiki branch text: 'Put yourself in stasis for 2.5 seconds, rendering you untargetable and invulnerable for the duration but also unable to move, declare basic attacks, cast abilities, use summoner spells, or activate items.' Outgoing damage during the window is not increased - it is strictly suppressed (no attacks, no abilities). Durability during the window is unbounded (invulnerable). So d(TDD)/d(item) <= 0, never > 0.
step_2_does_the_mechanic_touch_outgoing_.conclusion: For every candidate, the represented mechanic is an incoming-damage/survivability mechanic and adds nothing to outgoing TDD. The substantive claim shared by the old and new strings is CORRECT.

step_3_is_the_new_universal_clause_true.claim_under_test: 'Every declared family on this item is a defence.'
step_3_is_the_new_universal_clause_true.Banshee's Veil / Verdant Barrier: Declared effect families = {heal-shield} only; all three atoms are shield/shield-magic/heal-and-shield-power. Every one is a defence. TRUE.
step_3_is_the_new_universal_clause_true.Zhonya's Hourglass / Seeker's Armguard: Declared effect families = {crowd-control-mobility, damage}. The crowd-control-mobility atom is 'crowd-control-mobility.stasis' (self-stasis = durability). The 'damage'-family atom is 'damage.resistance-mitigation' - mitigation of INCOMING damage on the holder, not an outgoing-damage term. The atom taxonomy names families by mechanic kind, not by direction; both atoms here are defences. TRUE.
step_3_is_the_new_universal_clause_true.falsifiability_check: The clause is not vacuous - it excludes real items. Abyssal Mask (8020) declares family 'damage' via 'Unmake': 'Enemy champions within 700 units of you become cursed, causing them to receive 12% increased magic damage from all sources.' That is an outgoing-TDD amplifier sitting on an MR/health item. Under the OLD wording ('the represented mechanic changes defense') a coverage entry for such an item could read as justified from its defensive stat line alone; the NEW wording forces the check over every declared family and would fail loudly. The new sentence is the strictly stronger, checkable form, and it holds for the whole defence-only candidate set.

step_4_terminology.durability: 'Durability' is a first-class term in the cached wiki index (data/wiki/article-index.json, page 'Durability', pageid 961552), and is the precise word for the quantity these mechanics move (survivability against incoming damage), whereas 'defense' colloquially reads as the armor/MR stat pair. docs/math-foundations.md Sec. 2.1 gives the durability identity the engine uses: raw = post*(1+R/100), EHP(R) = H0*(1+R/100) - a target-side quantity that appears nowhere in the outgoing damage sum.
step_4_terminology.TDD: 'Outgoing TDD' = total damage dealt by the attacker. No formula in docs/math-foundations.md places a self-shield, self-stasis, or incoming-mitigation term in the outgoing damage path; mitigation m(R) is applied to the DEFENDER's resistances, so a holder-side durability effect cannot enter the attacker's TDD.

independent_computation.result: The correct reason is the new value. Both strings assert the same true core fact, so the old value is not factually false - but it is the weaker, unsourced form: it asserts only that 'the represented mechanic' is defensive, without establishing that nothing else on the item feeds outgoing TDD. The new value states the actual sufficient condition (every declared family is a defence), which is exactly what the cached atom decomposition supports for every item that can carry this verdict, and uses the wiki's own term 'durability'.

caveats: The concrete item named by item_coverage[0] could not be resolved from the evidence tree (scenario is engine-generated and absent from data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json). The verdict is therefore established over the complete set of mage-legal items whose declared effect families are all defences - the only items that can produce this reason - rather than against a single named item.

If the engine ever emits this reason for an item that declares an outgoing-damage family (e.g. Abyssal Mask's 'Unmake'), the NEW string would be false and the finding would flip to both_wrong. Nothing in the cached data indicates that case; the new string is precisely the guard against it.
